newsitem.title: INDIA: Cosmetic sops will sour Indian bourses-brokers.
newsitem.headline: Cosmetic sops will sour Indian bourses-brokers.

text.p: India's bubbling stock markets will take a beating if morale-boosting new measures promised by the government this week turn out to be cosmetic changes, brokers said on Wednesday.
"The market would react negatively," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange. "This is a choppy market driven by bouts of frenzy."

Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is scheduled to consider a stock lending scheme, an amendment in the country's share depository act, a report on short sales and a new takeover code, a SEBI official said.
SEBI chief D.R. Mehta on Wednesday met Montek Singh Alhuwalia, the most senior bureaucrat in the finance ministry, ahead of SEBI's board meeting.
Traders said on the items on SEBI's agenda were long-awaited proposals and will not be sufficient to satisfy expectations.
People are hoping for tax breaks on company dividends, buy-back of shares by companies, easing carry-forward rules for stock markets and changes in a controversial minimum tax on firms.
"I'm very sceptical," one broker said. "The government has very little leeway -- it is caught between the rock and a hard place."
The government on Wednesday played down expectations that a large package of measures to spur financial markets would be announced this week, saying its efforts were more broadly focused.

"The capital market is an important segment. The government effort is to move on a very broad front so the economy picks up in all sectors, not just the capital market," he told Reuters in Delhi by telephone.

Other government officials said the financial markets may have become overly optimistic that the federal government would unveil a single package of measures by the end of the month to strengthen investors' confidence.
On Wednesday the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange index fell 78.36 points, or 2.17 percent, to 3,525.84 at provisional close.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had said on Monday that some decisions could be expected before he left on Friday for Davos in Switzerland to attend a meeting of the World Economic Forum.
